dialog.body: Public Works, this is Denise, how can I help you?
Hi, yeah, um, hi. I'm calling about the storm drain by my parents' house. The basement flooded again and I'm, honestly I'm kind of nervous about what's going on with it.
Okay, I'm sorry to hear that. Let's get it down. What's the address?
So it's my mother's house, she's the owner, I live there with them, I'm her son. Oh, sorry, you asked the address. It's 31 Howard Street. Fifth Ward, down toward the corner where the drain is.
31 Howard. And your name?
Min-jun Okafor. M-I-N, dash, J-U-N. Okafor, O-K-A-F-O-R.

Okafor, Howard Street. Hang on, that rings a bell. Give me one second. [pause] Yup, here it is. Priya Okafor called in January, the twelfth. That was me, actually, I took that one. Drain backup at the corner.

Yeah, that's my mom. That was the first time. That was the storm in January, Friday night into Saturday, the tenth. And now it's happened again. Second time this winter. This weekend, with the nor'easter.
Okay. When did the water come in, do you know?

It was bad Saturday, like all day the wind was crazy. Sorry, you mean the basement. Overnight. Saturday night into Sunday. I went down maybe two in the morning because I heard the sump, well, I thought I heard something, and there was already water on the floor.
How much water are we talking?
About eight inches. I put a tape measure in it. Last time was like three. So it's, I mean, it more than doubled. That's what's freaking me out a little.
Eight inches. And where's it getting in?

Same spots as January. The window well on the street side, the glass, it comes in right around the glass, and then the bulkhead door. Nothing new. It's the exact same two places. Which, I don't know, I guess that tells you something.
It does. Window well glass, street side, and the bulkhead. Same as the first time.
Right.
And what was the street doing? Was the drain backed up?

The street was a river. My dad was looking out the front, he was like, come look at this. It was ankle deep out there, easy. And cars were still driving through it, they were throwing these wakes, like boats, and it was washing right up toward the house. Toward that window well. I wanted to go out and wave people down but it was the middle of the night, so.
Yeah, that doesn't help. Was the grate at the corner covered, could you see it?

I couldn't see it at all. Just water. Um, actually my car's parked right there, and I was trying to see if it was in the water, and, this is dumb, but my parking sticker, the residential one? It keeps peeling off the glass. I've stuck it back on like three times. And I'm out there in the rain with a flashlight thinking great, now I'm gonna get a ticket on top of everything. Sorry. Not your department. The grate, no, I couldn't see the grate.

That's all right. Lot of people with that sticker issue, honestly, the cold doesn't help. But for the sticker you'd want to call the parking office, not us. Okay, so the drain. After your mom's call in January, I have a crew going out on the thirteenth. Did somebody come?

Yeah, Tuesday. They came and they cleaned off the grate. Like leaves and junk on top. My mom said they were there maybe, I don't know, not long. And that was it. Nobody did anything under the street, they just cleared the top. And I'm not, I'm not trying to say they did a bad job, I just, if it's something underneath, then clearing the leaves isn't going to do it, right? And now it's worse.
That's fair. What I've got here says the grate was cleared, that's it.

Yeah. And the neighbor, a couple houses down on our side, same thing. Both times. January and this weekend. He told me Sunday morning, he was out there with a shop vac. So it's not just us, it's like the whole low spot there.
Okay, that's helpful, I'll put that in. Neighbor on Howard also had water both storms. Now inside, what got damaged?

So the basement's finished, mostly. But the, um, the part that got it, it's the same stuff as last time. Paint cans, ladders, and my mom has all these boxes of our school things, like from when we were kids, report cards and drawings and stuff. Those got wet again. She was pretty upset. Nothing new though. Same stuff as January, just wetter.
Same items, nothing additional.

Right. But that's kind of my worry. The freezer and the washer and dryer are down there too, and the rec room, and they were fine this time. But it went from three to eight. If it goes up again, the next one, I don't know. I'm an electrician, I'm thinking about the outlets down there, the panel, and I'm like, I don't love this. My parents are getting older, I don't want my dad wading around down there with stuff plugged in.
No, that's a real concern. If water's ever up near outlets, you keep everybody out of there, but you know that better than me.
Yeah, no, I shut the breaker for down there Sunday. Sorry, that's not what you asked. Go ahead.

No, good, that's smart. Okay. So here's what I'm going to do. I'm logging this as a repeat backup, same location, so it's tied to your mom's January report and it doesn't just look like a brand new call.

Okay. Can I, is there any way to get somebody higher up to actually look at it? Like a supervisor, or an engineer, somebody who'd know if the pipe's the problem? Because I feel like if another crew just comes and cleans the grate, we're gonna be doing this again in a month.

Yup, I was getting there. I'm putting in for a crew to go out Wednesday, that's the twenty-fifth, and I'm flagging it so they look at the line, not just the top. And I'm requesting a supervisor call you back. That should happen by Thursday, the twenty-sixth. The supervisor can decide if engineering needs to get involved.
Wednesday. Okay. Will they need to get in the house or anything?
They'll be working at the corner, in the street. They shouldn't need anything from you. If somebody's home and wants to tell them where the water was sitting, that never hurts.
My dad'll probably be out there watching them anyway. [pause] Sorry. Okay, the supervisor, should they call me or my mom?
That's up to you. Who's easiest to get?
I'm on job sites all day, but I pick up. My mom's at the school. Me. Call me.
What's a good number for you?
It's 401-555-0168. That's my cell.
401-555-0168. And that's Min-jun, M-I-N dash J-U-N.
That's it.

Okay. Let me read back what I've got, make sure it's right. 31 Howard Street. Basement flooded overnight Saturday into Sunday, about eight inches. Water came in at the street-side window well glass and the bulkhead door, same as the January flood, which was about three inches. Second flood this winter. Street was ankle deep, cars pushing water toward the house. Neighbor had water both storms. Paint cans, ladders, and boxes of school things wet again, nothing else. Crew in January cleared the grate only. Requesting someone look at the line under the corner, crew Wednesday, supervisor callback by Thursday.
Yeah. That's, yeah. That's all of it.
Good.
Can I ask, um, is there something we should be doing in the meantime? Because there's supposed to be more rain at some point, right? It's still February. I keep looking at the forecast.

I hear you. Some people put sandbags against the bulkhead, that can buy you a little. And if you see the street filling up again, call us right away, even if it's the middle of the night, that goes to dispatch and they can send somebody out. Don't wait till morning.
Okay. Sandbags. I didn't think of the bulkhead, I was so focused on the window. Okay.
And the window well, if there's a cover you can get over it, that helps keep the street water off the glass.
Yeah. I'll look into that tonight. I'm sorry, I'm a little all over the place, I barely slept the last two nights.
You're fine. You've had a weekend.
Yeah. [pause] And if the supervisor doesn't call by Thursday?
Then you call me back Friday and ask for Denise, and I'll chase it. Your mom's call and yours are tied together now, so whoever picks up can pull it right up.
Okay. Okay, thank you. I just really don't want this to be a third time.
I understand. We'll get eyes on it. Go eat some lunch, try and get some sleep tonight.
I'll try. Thanks, Denise.
You're welcome. Bye now.
